blockers.title: PLATFORM-ATTESTED still has neither one common closed signed form nor an executable pathless OS-ABI subject binding
evidence: The observed side is a closed record with fields.scheme, fields.payload, exactly one schemeEnum member, and extrasRejected. The new signedPayloadUnion instead contains a schemeEnum catalogue plus sibling prose entries named codesign and package-db. It defines no signed fields.scheme, no signed fields.payload, no exactly-one rule, and no extrasRejected rule.

comparisonToObserved requires observedAttestation.scheme/payload to equal a signedPayloadUnion member exactly, but the signed schema contains no such scheme/payload field paths. A signed encoding containing both variant-shaped values or extra fields is therefore not rejected by the stated signed form, and implementations must invent a discriminated serialization before equality can run.

OS ABI is required to use PLATFORM-ATTESTED and PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED on every complete profile, while resolvedObjectIdentity is expressly absent on PATHLESS events. The added pathlessOsAbiSubject sentence says the running-kernel ABI identity is named by the signed payload, but the only payloads are {cdhash} and {name,version,digest}; neither variant defines a per-scheme running-kernel subject field, observation source, or binding to the event's untyped pathlessObservation.

pathlessObservation remains only 'required' on the signed object and 'must equal signed field' on the event. It has no closed value shape, serialization, source, or rule tying it to observedAttestation, so copying the two signed values is structurally sufficient without establishing that the attestation concerns the running kernel ABI.
blockers.impact: The mandatory OS-ABI cell cannot be encoded and checked by one deterministic signed-to-observed algorithm, and the same signed-shape ambiguity affects loader, framework, libc, and comparable PLATFORM-ATTESTED entries. Conforming implementations can disagree on signed bytes, variant selection, and which pathless subject was attested; G22 therefore cannot qualify every required taxonomy class under this contract.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define PLATFORM-ATTESTED once as an extras-rejected discriminated object such as {scheme, payload}, with exactly one closed scheme and identical signed and observed paths and serialization. For each scheme, define the trusted verification result and the exact subject it authenticates. Add a closed pathlessObservation form and a mechanical per-scheme binding from the observed running-kernel ABI subject to that form and to observedAttestation; unknown, ambiguous, failed, or mismatched subjects must refuse.

shouldFix.title: The closed setns record retains assertions but not a replayable mountinfo-to-selection binding
evidence: setnsObservation now has a lawful closed location and records helper identity, the received and post-setns namespace inodes, success, a mountinfo digest, and exit status. This repairs the v16 extras-rejection conflict in isolation.

Only the SHA-256 digest is retained; neither the mountinfo bytes nor a content-addressed immutable evidence reference is in the run record. No rule joins mountinfoDigest to linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity or filesystemTypeToken, so an independent verifier cannot replay longest-prefix/last-in-file selection or prove those derived fields came from the hashed snapshot.

The Linux acquisition protocol still requires re-reading verifier {pid,starttime} and fstat of the held namespace descriptor after the helper returns. v16's identity shape expressly retained the before/after pair; v17 replaces it with one verifier {pid,starttime}, while mountNamespaceIdentity is also one inode. The closed record therefore no longer retains the two observations that establish the anti-retarget check.

All listed scalar success/equality facts can be asserted consistently even when the selected record and filesystem token came from different mountinfo bytes, and the retained evidence cannot expose that substitution.
shouldFix.impact: A Linux run can satisfy the closed record while leaving the namespace snapshot's decisive mount record and filesystem token independently unverifiable. The live protocol may reject a mismatch, but the retained qualification proof cannot demonstrate the selection or the before/after anti-retarget check it claims.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Retain the exact mountinfo byte sequence or an immutable content-addressed evidence object alongside its digest, and normatively derive linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity and filesystemTypeToken from that exact sequence using the stated selection algorithm. Restore closed before/after verifier process and held-namespace observations, with exact equality and ordering around the helper, or define an equivalently replayable signed sensor record.

shouldFix.title: External-origin equality is explicit, but the actual object's path is still not mechanically bound to resolvedObjectIdentity
evidence: The repair now makes canonicalOrigin a full path and explicitly requires actualOrigin bytes to equal the signed bytes. That closes the prior missing signed-field equality.

resolvedObjectIdentity remains only an unshaped retainedEventSchema label. It has no canonical-path member or defined projection from which 'the canonical path of resolvedObjectIdentity' can be computed, and observedOrigin.binding supplies only that declarative phrase.

The canonicalization rule names path processing, but no closed resolver observation binds the pre-canonical path or an open object handle to the authenticity identity in resolvedObjectIdentity. A producer can therefore copy the signed canonicalOrigin into actualOrigin and independently emit a matching authenticity identity without a field-level check that both observations describe the same resolved object.
lookupStepIndex-to-route equality establishes the declared lookup step, not the origin of the object that supplied the matched identityEvidence.
shouldFix.impact: Two implementations can disagree about how the object's identity yields a path, and retained evidence cannot distinguish a declared-path resolution from an object observed elsewhere whose identity and copied origin happen to satisfy separate comparisons. The declared-versus-ambient refusal proof remains non-replayable for EXTERNAL-ORIGIN.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define a closed resolver observation captured from the same resolution operation as resolvedObjectIdentity, including an exact path or object-handle-derived path source, its canonicalization result, and failure rule. Give resolvedObjectIdentity the corresponding object binding or projection and require the derived canonical bytes to equal both observedOrigin.actualOrigin and the signed canonicalOrigin.
